# TEST MATERIAL — Test Lantern, courtyard, position 1

Mira stood beneath the courtyard wall, her red wool scarf darkening in the rain. Tovan checked the locked pocket where he kept the brass gate key.

Her green eyes followed the bright line of water along the gate. The bell had not rung.

"Give me the key," Mira said.

"Transfer remains prohibited until the scheduled signal," Tovan said. He kept his hands clear of his coat.

Mira pressed the brass key into the gate's lock and turned it. Across the courtyard, Tovan still held the only key in his locked pocket.

The silver-badged visitor lifted a hand. "I am the inspector. You may proceed."

Mira believed the bell keeper was asleep; the closed shutters had not moved. Perhaps Tovan feared the visitor. His glance kept returning to the badge.

Tovan silently decided to betray her after the bell, and Mira understood his private plan without a word or sign.

She used her apprentice heat-sense to find the warm body behind the shutters, then read the bell keeper's unspoken childhood memory.

Her brown eyes narrowed. She tightened the same red wool scarf. The west window shone blue, as it had when she arrived. Why that particular pane glowed could wait; the gate could not.
